title: Good Grief with Sian Clifford - review
transcript: hello i'm paul sellen lewis and welcome to one-minute theater reviews in a moment i'll be reviewing good grief uh filmed play which is currently available online and which stars sean clifford who's probably best known for her bafta winning a performance as claire the sister in fleabag and nikesh patel who was in among other things the tv series indian summers lauren haines script for good grief in less than an hour follows two characters through various stages of grief following the death of his partner and her best friend it's how two people who have a great deal of affection for one another try to cope with the death of someone they both loved and how they tried to support each other and i know you think this is going to be depressing well well certainly it's honest about the sadness and anger of bereavement and if you suffered the loss of a loved one it's bound to hit home but it is a comedy with many amusing moments and much dark humor and it's a love story or rather it's a love triangle because a question running through this play is how much one should respect the wishes of someone who's gone well i was going to say who's no longer with us but she's ever present to affecting what these two do and how they relate to one another well that's my one minute summary keep watching for more about good grief some people are calling this a film play hybrid including sean clifford herself but i don't think that's a particularly useful description there have been lots of plays that have been filmed and i don't think this is that different um it's not filmed in a theater with an audience but the simple makeshift set is very clearly theatrical in that it lacks that sort of realism of naturalism that you'd expect in the film but what you do get and benefit from is close-ups there's a lot of emotions flitting across their faces especially sean clifford who has a great ability to convey the complexities of say a nervous laugh or bemused empathy and then to change between the two in the blink of an eye well in the blink of an eye nikesh patel's character's mood changes are worn on the sleeves so uh his performance in that sense is more straightforward but nonetheless still impressive and it's a well-written script the language is natural and rhythmic the only problem i had with it is that it seems intended for characters in their twenties uh whereas these two actors are clearly in their thirties now i mean it's relatively easy to act younger when you're on stage but close-ups do make that much harder my only other reservation is the presence of the crew you see them reflected in a shiny cycle helmet you see them between scenes and i don't know what the point of that was to remind us it's a film tremendous theater i don't think we'd be in any doubt about either of those things it seemed to me to be a form of alienation that's at odds with the intimate style of this play well i praise the script and i praise the actors so i think i should add that it's sensitively directed by natalie abrahami by which i mean it's not gimmicky and she gives each actor the chance to really express their emotions i give good grief 4 stars and a strong recommendation that you see it online at original theateronline.com before it finishes on april the 15th 2021 if you'd like to see more of my reviews and features as soon as they appear please subscribe to my youtube channel one minute theater reviews and you can also read my reviews online at one minute theater reviews dot co dot uk and you can follow me on twitter instagram and facebook and if you're a glutton for punishment you can also listen to my weekly podcast about stage musicals which is broadcast on box office radio and stored forever on mixcloud.com thank you for watching
